content.user_title: Build Azure File Share Workflows in TypeScript
content.value_statement: Azure File Share SDK workflows require precise client, authentication, and transfer patterns. This skill provides focused TypeScript examples for common storage operations.
actual_capabilities: Explains connection strings, shared keys, managed identity, and SAS authentication.
Shows how to create, list, inspect, configure, and delete shares.
Covers directory creation, listing, existence checks, and deletion.
Demonstrates file uploads, downloads, copies, metadata, headers, and range operations.
Provides snapshot creation, access, deletion, and SAS generation patterns.
Documents Node.js and browser capability differences.
limitations: Provides guidance and examples, but does not execute Azure operations.
Requires an existing Azure account, storage account, and appropriate permissions.
Examples use placeholder names and paths that need environment-specific validation.
Does not cover infrastructure provisioning, SMB mounting, monitoring, or cost analysis.

use_cases.title: Build File Transfer Services
use_cases.description: Create reliable TypeScript upload and download flows for application files.

use_cases.title: Automate Share Administration
use_cases.description: Implement repeatable share, directory, quota, snapshot, and cleanup operations.

use_cases.title: Secure Storage Integrations
use_cases.description: Choose managed identity, shared key, connection string, or scoped SAS authentication.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Share
prompt_templates.prompt: Show a TypeScript example that authenticates with DefaultAzureCredential and creates an Azure file share named [share-name].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new file share.

prompt_templates.title: Upload a Local File
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Node.js TypeScript workflow to upload [local-path] into [share-name]/[directory-name] with clear error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Stream Large Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend an Azure File Share streaming upload design for files around [size], including buffer size, concurrency, retries, and validation.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Secure Storage Service
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production TypeScript service for uploads, downloads, snapshots, and read-only SAS links. Use managed identity and least privilege.

output_examples.input: How should a Node.js service upload a large local archive to Azure Files?
output: Use a file stream and obtain the local size before creating the remote file.
Set bounded concurrency and buffer sizes based on memory and network capacity.
Use managed identity where available, and handle Azure status codes explicitly.

output_examples.input: Which authentication method should a production Azure-hosted service use?
output_examples.output: Use DefaultAzureCredential with managed identity. Grant only required storage permissions and avoid storing shared keys in application configuration.

output_examples.input: How can a client receive temporary read access to one file?
output_examples.output: Generate a file-scoped SAS with read-only permission and a short expiration. Share the URL securely and never write it to logs.

best_practices: Prefer managed identity and least-privilege roles for production authentication.
Use streams for large files and validate paths, sizes, and transfer results.
Use short-lived, narrowly scoped SAS tokens and keep credential-bearing URLs out of logs.
anti_patterns: Do not embed account keys, connection strings, or SAS tokens in source code.
Do not accept unvalidated share names, file paths, or source URLs from users.
Do not use broad SAS permissions or long expiration periods without documented need.

faq.question: Does this skill create Azure resources automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides TypeScript guidance and examples that require your Azure environment and credentials.

faq.question: Which authentication method is preferred for production?
faq.answer: Use DefaultAzureCredential with managed identity when Azure hosting supports it.

faq.question: Can I use every example in a browser?
faq.answer: No. Shared key credentials, local file methods, buffers, streams, and SAS generation are Node.js features.

faq.question: Does the skill support large files?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents stream uploads, direct file downloads, ranges, buffering, and concurrency controls.

faq.question: Does it cover temporary file access?
faq.answer: Yes. It demonstrates file and share SAS generation with configurable permissions and expiration.

faq.question: What must I customize before using an example?
faq.answer: Replace account names, share names, directory names, file paths, permissions, quotas, and credential configuration.
